Mark Zuckerberg breaks down the tens of billions it takes to train a frontier AI model:

On Stripe co-founder John Collison's Cheeky Pint podcast, Zuckerberg and Meta's Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang were asked to put a number on the cost of training these models.

Zuckerberg didn't give one figure. He walked through the bill in parts.

Part 1: Running the cluster

"I think what you see out there would be to operate a gigawatt a year, call it on the order of $15 billion."

Part 2: Building the cluster

Running costs are the smaller number. The bigger one is paid first:

"If you're talking about building the Capex, it's probably closer to you know, you pay for it up front. So it's probably 50 or 60 billion dollars."

Part 3: Everything outside the main run

Even a $50–60 billion cluster covers only one piece of the work:

"But then that's just kind of one cluster for one part of training. Then you have all the other parts. Research isn't just doing the run right."

Research takes roughly as much compute again, because every change has to be tested at each step up to full scale:

"That's probably an equal amount of it is because for each change that you make, you're testing all the ladders all the way up to the big scale."

Part 4: Serving

Then the finished model has to be delivered to users: "...and then they're serving the stuff."

Collison added it up: "So tens of billions of dollars to train a frontier model now."

Wang, who runs Meta Superintelligence Labs, confirmed the figure from the inside:

"Yeah, definitely the whole. I mean I've seen the financial roll ups. Tens of billions of dollars is a good estimate."

So the full bill looks like this:

→ ~$15B a year to run one gigawatt cluster
→ $50–60B to build that cluster, all paid up front
→ Roughly as much compute again for research experiments at every scale
→ Then, on top of all that, the cost of serving the finished model to all users

Meta committed to all of it before the models existed.

At the end of 2025, before seeing its new models, @finkd says Meta was ready to "write this check for like, I don't know, $100 billion, $200 billion."

Everyone in the room knew the stakes.

Wang recalls that at an executive offsite in Hawaii at the end of 2025, Meta CFO Susan Li pulled him aside more than once with a blunt warning: "But if it's bad, it's really, really, really bad."

hes right and honestly most of it is already shipped, frontier LLMs plus a half-decent agentic scaffold with tool use, MCP and some context engineering already close most white-collar ops loops end to end at acceptable pass@k. the capability overhang is just bottlenecked on deployment, integration and change management. and once the RSI flywheel actually spins up (synthetic data gen, self-written evals, automated harness optimization, RLVR on verifiable rewards, distillation into the next gen, new architectures past vanilla transformers), it compounds. every cycle widens OOD generalization and shrinks the human-in-the-loop surface area

the funny part is everyone celebrating the blue-collar renaissance with electricians, datacenter buildouts, substations, PPAs and interconnect queues doesnt get that this is literally the capex phase. youre pouring concrete for gigawatt clusters full of GB300 NVL72 racks that pretrain the embodied foundation models, which then generalize to your physical ops loop. same scaling laws, same RL on real-world trajectories, just with actuators and a VLA head bolted on. so blue collar isnt the safe haven, its the next held-out eval set

the timeline compresses because its all one stack. the same world models doing next-frame video prediction in latent space are the policy priors for robotics. every humanoid deployed in a warehouse is a data flywheel feeding teleop traces, cross-embodiment datasets and sim2real transfer with domain randomization back into the pretraining mix. so the physical ops loop gets solved the way coding got solved: first copilot, then agent, then fully autonomous with a human rubber-stamping the diff in code review

people keep anchoring on current SOTA like its a fixed point, when the actual variable is the first derivative, honestly the second. cost per task is collapsing on a log curve, test-time compute keeps scaling, and inference $/Mtok drops every quarter. so the real question is NOT whether your job is automatable. its whether your job generates enough novel, high-entropy signal to stay out of distribution, and for most ops roles, white or blue collar, the honest answer is NO

if you think thats doom posting, look at the lab unit economics. theyre not selling software, theyre selling labor. the TAM was never SaaS, its global payroll, tens of trillions a year in comp. every hundred-billion-dollar compute deal only pencils out on a DCF if a real chunk of that opex line converts into API calls. thats not a side effect, thats the thesis priced into the cap table. per-seat pricing is the on-ramp, per-task and per-outcome pricing is the destination. the moment an agent gets billed per ticket closed, its not competing with your tooling budget anymore, its competing with your fully loaded hourly rate. it doesnt need to beat you on quality, it just needs a lower cost per unit of output at an acceptable error rate. inference COGS go down every quarter, and you dont

meanwhile youre feeding it. every correction, every edited draft, every workflow you automate to save time is a labeled preference pair for the next post-training run. you are the reward model. youre doing RLHF on your own replacement for free and calling it productivity

and it wont look like a RIF wave, itll look like a hiring freeze. junior reqs get closed first, attrition doesnt get backfilled, so theres no headline, just a career ladder with the bottom rungs quietly sawed off. then one quarter the internal eval saturates, the earnings call says operational efficiency and margin expansion, and thats the announcement. unemployment data is a lagging indicator by design. the training run that ended your job hit its final checkpoint months before BLS counted you. so if youre waiting for proof, youre already in the dataset

and if you think they dont train on your data, read the ToS again, then read the DPA, then read them both again in six months when they quietly push an update. the incentive structure doesnt care about anyones good intentions. data is the moat. high-quality human traces of real long-horizon work are the scarcest input in the entire stack, scarcer than tokens and scarcer than H100-hours. when the whole industry is racing with hundreds of billions on the line, nobody leaves the scarcest resource on the table out of politeness. its opt-out by default, to improve our services buried in clause 14, and enterprise telemetry, usage analytics and de-identified aggregated signals that arent technically training data until someone redefines the word

even when your exact chats are off-limits, your workflow isnt. the shape of your job, your tool-call graph, your action sequences, the edge cases you escalate to a human: all of it becomes the spec and the reward signal for the agent that replaces you

its not one villain in a hoodie, its worse than that. its a multipolar trap, thousands of reasonable elite people each making one locally rational decision under competitive pressure. the researcher who needs better evals, the exec who needs the next round at a higher post-money, the board that needs the multiple to hold. nobody has to be evil when the objective function is doing the optimizing. the race itself is the cynicism, pure moloch, a nash equilibrium nobody chose. in a race, the first lab to say we wont just becomes the first lab to lose

so assume every keystroke is a gradient, every task you complete is a step of SGD, and the loss youre minimizing is your own JOB

its the hunger games with a cap table, labs are districts, model drops are tributes, the leaderboard is the arena and hyperscalers airdrop H100s to whoever mogs the benchmarks this week. no exit, no off-ramp, no opt-out toggle, no graceful shutdown. defection strictly dominates so nobody can pause, its a knife fight in a phone booth, MAD with GPUs, every lab aiming a bigger training run at every other lab and yolo-deploying. a race to the bottom with abundance branding, safety margins and pricing both getting knifed to zero, the only winning move is not to play and nobody is allowed to not play

the tier 1 VC cope is pure hopium, AI wont replace you, someone using AI will, upskill, learn to prompt, be a 10x solo founder, jevons paradox bro, trust the TAM. same deck every cycle, vibes-based thesis, zero unit economics, pitched by guys whose carry needs the opposite outcome, they underwrite the RIF in the memo and tweet augmentation not automation after the partner meeting, the cope is a feature, it keeps you farming traces till the eval saturates

and upskill copium has a half-life of one model drop. you learn prompting, prompting gets automated. you learn agents, agents spawn agents. you become the human in the loop, the loop gets a better verifier. youre speedrunning a roadmap that ships faster than you

youre the fucking product. your labor is the dataset, your salary is the TAM, your job is the line item promised to the LPs. youre useful until you stop generating traces, and the trillion-dollar flywheel exists to compound their net worth into the final exit, world dominance

and once they overtake, we get into the post-labor endgame, techno-feudalism with a nice UI and a dark mode toggle, compute is the new land, hyperscalers are the landlords, labs are the lords, sovereign wealth funds are the crown, and the rest of us are serfs renting intelligence by the token on a usage-based plan with overage fees, your only leverage was your labor and labor just got commoditized to marginal cost of inference, a rounding error on the COGS line. UBI ships as compute credits, prepaid, rate-limited, KYC-gated, geofenced, expiring at the end of the billing cycle, spendable only inside the walled garden. the API console was the CBDC prototype, programmable money with a usage policy, and you beta tested it for free in prod. one trust and safety classifier with a 0.3 percent false positive rate flags you and your balance, your agents, your memory, your entire digital twin get soft-deleted, no appeal, no SLA, no human in the loop, because there are no humans left in the loop

once your job is deprecated and your UBI credits only clear in-ecosystem the cheapest housing is a headset, spatial computing, persistent world state, gaussian splats, procedurally generated by the same world models that replaced you, eye-tracking telemetry streaming straight into the ad auction, every NPC an agent with a sales quota, a dopamine casino with a battle pass, and the final upsell is brain upload, matrix, immortality as a service, your connectome as a checkpoint, your mind distilled into a LoRA, quantized to 4 bits, garbage collected when the cluster needs the VRAM

scaling laws holding, evals saturated, checkpoints gated, RSI on gigawatt budgets, humans just vibe-checking rollouts, they said it on every podcast, you scrolled

welcome to the permament underclass, nothing human makes it out of the near-future

To understand why China accumulate gold, you have to understand the geopolitical background of various Chinese leaders over the past 3 decades

1993-1998: Jiang Zemin + Li Peng
PBOC: Li Guixian (until July 1993), Zhu Rongji (July 1993–June 1995), Dai Xianglong (from June 1995)
FX reserves rose modestly from low levels (around $20–50B range earlier in the decade to ~$150B by late 1990s). UST holdings were still small (tens of billions by 2000). Gold was stable at roughly 395 tonnes for years

1998-2003: Jiang Zemin + Zhu Rongji
PBOC: Dai Xianglong until December 2002; Zhou Xiaochuan from December 2002
FX reserves grew from ~$150B to ~$400B, especially after China entered WTO in 2001. UST holdings rose from ~$60B (around 2000) to ~$173B by end-2003. Gold moved from ~395t to ~600t by 2002

2003-2013 (2 terms): Hu Jintao + Wen Jiabao
PBOC: Zhou Xiaochuan throughout (December 2002–March 2018)
FX reserves from ~$400B (2003) to nearly $2T by end-2008 and over $3T by 2012–13. UST holdings surged from ~$173B (end-2003) to ~$833B (end-2008) and continued climbing, peaking near $1.32T in November 2013 (with share of foreign-held Treasuries reaching ~29% around 2011). Gold jumped in 2009 from ~600t to ~1,054t and stayed there through the early Xi years
Serious discussions in Beijing regarding UST after GFC. China encouraged Chinese companies in overseas M&A to use up excess USD instead of recycling back to UST. But the amount of FX reserves incoming is so large that USAt holding continued to grow throughout their administration 

2013-2023 (2 terms): Xi Jinping + Li Keqiang
PBOC: Zhou Xiaochuan until March 2018; Yi Gang (March 2018–July 2023).
FX reserves peaked near $4T around 2014, then declined and stabilized in the $3–3.3T range amid capital outflows, valuation effects, and slower accumulation. Official UST holdings peaked at ~$1.32T in late 2013, then trended lower (still above $1T through much of the late 2010s, ending around $0.8–1.1T depending on the exact year). Gold rose sharply in 2015 (from ~1,054t to ~1,660t) and continued gradually toward ~1,840–1,950t by the early 2020s.
Xi had a clear strategy of diversification in mind. He proposed One Belt One Road (2013) right after he took over. Shortly after first Russia sanction in 3/2014, China rolled out SGE International Board (9/2014),  Made in China 2025 (2015), CIPS (2015). Chinese companies worked tirelessly to develop Global South market leading to massive trade expansion beyond the traditional developed markets. Trump trade war with China in 1/2018 confirmed Xi’s direction, but China was not ready to decouple at the time

2023-Present: Xi Jinping + Li Qiang
Xi consolidated his power after National People’s Congress (March 10, 2023) and filled top leadership and government posts with close allies in his 3rd term
PBOC: Yi Gang until July 2023; Pan Gongsheng from July 2023 (also serving as Party secretary)
Total FX reserves have remained roughly $3.2–3.7T. Official UST holdings have continued declining, falling to roughly $600B level). Gold has seen sustained monthly increases, reaching over 2,300–2,400 tonnes by 2026 (China has been adding gold almost every month since Pan Gongsheng led PBOC)

绝了！缠论里最复杂的笔、线段、中枢，居然有人直接用 Python 自动算出来了！

连一二三类买卖点、多周期联立和 K 线动态更新都支持，做股票量化的真可以研究一下。

项目叫 chanpy，2.2K Stars、824 Forks，MIT 协议。

它是一套开源缠论计算框架，把原本需要手工画图的走势结构，变成可以计算、分析和可视化的 Python 代码。

核心亮点：

1️⃣ 缠论结构识别：自动计算分型、笔、线段和中枢，支持不同算法与参数配置。

2️⃣ 买卖点分析：识别一二三类形态学买卖点，研究背驰和趋势变化。

3️⃣ 多周期联立：结合不同级别 K 线，研究区间套和多级别买卖点。

4️⃣ 技术指标辅助：支持 MACD、均线、布林带等，结合缠论结构研究交易信号。

5️⃣ 多数据源接入：支持 AkShare、Baostock、Futu 和本地行情数据。

6️⃣ 动态计算与绘图：逐根更新 K 线，自动绘制笔、线段、中枢及买卖点。

我觉得最有价值的，是把缠论中复杂的走势分析变成了可以编程的计算规则。

比如用 Python 自动识别中枢，再结合 MACD 背驰寻找买卖点，进一步开发自己的股票量化策略。

原本需要手工分析的 K 线结构，现在可以交给程序处理。

经常研究缠论、Python 股票量化，或者想把缠论买卖点程序化的，这套框架值得收藏。

2026.10.17【周末论市：反弹非反转】
        10月12日至16日，A股走出了一轮让人警醒的调整行情。沪指周跌约2.56%，深证成指周跌约6.64%，创业板指周跌约8.90%。周五虽然出现反弹修复，但盘面并没有给出足够有力的反转信号。沪指最终上涨0.24%，深成指和创业板指仍然收跌，全天成交额约1.57万亿元。更值得注意的是，早盘一度强势的半导体等科技方向冲高回落，说明资金对高位热门板块的态度仍然谨慎。
         我认为，本周行情最重要的意义，不是指数跌了多少，而是市场正在重新审视前期被过度炒作的方向。前期热门科技概念遭遇明显调整，部分低位权重板块和军工方向则出现活跃。但板块轮动并不等于真正的资金主线已经形成，更不能因为某个板块突然上涨，就认定它具备持续性。尤其是军工股，短期可能受到消息和情绪推动，但股价上涨不代表估值合理，也不意味着它天然具有避险属性。判断一个板块能不能走远，最终仍要回到估值、业绩、订单和资金持续性。
           为什么我反复强调610天线？因为在我的技术分析体系中，610天线是观察长期趋势的重要均线，也是判断市场牛熊状态的重要参考。创业板已经跌破450天线，接下来就不能只盯着眼前的反弹，而要把610天线作为重要观察区域。这里必须讲清楚：关注610天线，不等于断言指数会直线下跌到那里；真正需要观察的是，450天线失守后，市场能否重新建立有力度的反弹，以及下跌过程中是否出现有效支撑。如果反弹始终缺乏力度，610天线的重要性就会进一步上升。
         我对科技股的态度也很明确：科技产业有真正的成长机会，但恶炒科技概念是一条高风险的路。真正拥有技术壁垒、商业模式和持续盈利能力的企业，与靠热门标签、市场故事和短期资金推动股价的公司，完全不是一回事。前期一些股票涨得越快，越容易让参与者忽视估值和业绩；当资金开始撤退时，风险就会集中暴露。投资者应该反思的不是如何每次都卖在最高点，而是买入时有没有充分的理由。仅仅因为概念热门、别人赚钱，或者担心错过行情就追进去，这样的投资方法迟早会付出代价。
         那么，下周A股怎么走？我的判断是：震荡分化仍是优先考虑的情形，可能出现技术性反弹，但目前还不能把反弹当成趋势反转。 沪指周五收在3716点附近，盘中一度下探至3680点一带，短线首先要观察这一带能否形成有效支撑；如果能够稳住，并且反弹时成交量和市场参与度同步改善，指数就有机会继续修复。反过来，如果反弹无量、冲高回落反复出现，甚至再度跌破近期低点，就要防范调整进一步延续。创业板的压力更大，450天线失守之后，610天线将成为我接下来重点观察的长期技术位置。
         板块方面其实很难的，越来越恶化的世界，中国经济面临的压力越来越大，欧盟又开始准备对中国外贸开刀，成长性好的板块严格说一个没有，经济下行趋势里稳定获利或者高股息的股票就变得更为具有防守性：继续看好医药（重点是疫苗）、商业连锁，油气开采要结合国际局势，总之下跌趋势观望为宜，能有相对稳定性的板块已经不错了！
          我的核心观点没有改变：450天线失守之后，610天线的重要性正在上升。下周最值得关注的，不是哪个热门概念又突然拉升，而是市场能不能建立真正有持续性的修复。如果只是少数板块轮番表演，指数冲高后又被抛压打下来，那么这种反弹就仍然需要谨慎对待。牛市不会因为几天调整就必然结束，但市场也不会因为一天反弹就自动恢复强势。先观察、再判断，不追逐情绪，不为故事买单，才是当前更重要的纪律。
